systemSummary.name: Kestra Event-Driven Declarative Orchestrator
systemSummary.description: Event-driven workflow orchestration platform using declarative YAML definitions, queue-based actor communication (Kafka / JDBC), and decoupled blob storage.

executionEngine.description: Stateful Executor consuming execution events, evaluating flowable task DAGs, and dispatching WorkerTasks.

workerLayer.description: Stateless Worker agents polling WorkerTasks, executing task runners (Docker, Process, Kubernetes), and outputting WorkerTaskResults.

queueLayer.description: Asynchronous messaging bus decoupling Executor, Worker, and Scheduler instances.

storageLayer.description: Durable blob storage for inter-task artifact passing using kestra:// URIs.

durableExecutionModel.eventDrivenQueues: Executors and Workers communicate strictly via asynchronous typed Queues. State is reconstructed from execution stream messages.
durableExecutionModel.flowableDAGs: DAG and parallel task execution is orchestrated by Flowable task handlers emitting next executable task runs as prior tasks complete.
durableExecutionModel.storageIsolation: Large inputs/outputs are written to StorageInterface, preventing memory bloating in message queues.
durableExecutionModel.concurrencySLA: Global and flow-level concurrency limits use atomic database/queue counters, fenced against double slot release on SLA timeouts.
durableExecutionModel.deadlockResilience: JDBC database wrappers detect nested SQL deadlock exceptions and perform automated transaction retries.
